feed.title: Combined summary - SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)

entry.title: Combined summary - SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
entry.summary: SHRINCS represents a significant development in the field of post-quantum cryptographic signature schemes for Bitcoin, offering a semi-stateful hash-based approach intended to enhance both compactness and verification speed. The proposal introduces public keys as small as 48 bytes and signatures ranging from 548 to 5777 bytes, depending on whether they are stateful or stateless. Security approximations align with NIST-I standards, leveraging truncated SHA256 believed to be robust against quantum adversaries. Verification efficiency is a key advantage, with SHRINCS signatures verifying between four and sixteen times faster than BIP340 Schnorr signatures, especially when SHA256 hardware acceleration is available. However, SHRINCS demands sophisticated management of an incrementing state counter for its stateful operation, where any mismanagement can lead to severe vulnerabilities like signature forgery. Key generation and signing remain computationally intensive but may benefit from optimizations such as SIMD, parallelism, or dedicated hardware. Recent advancements have expanded SHRINCS’ interoperability beyond Bitcoin, ensuring black-box compatibility with SLH-DSA algorithms and offering flexible parameter sets suitable for high-frequency signing environments, including applications like the Lightning Network. Despite these enhancements, the current draft lacks comprehensive test vectors, unit tests, formal security proofs, or optimized implementations, and does not conform to expected documentation formats. The development team is inviting community feedback through their [GitHub repository](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/blob/main/SHRINCS.md) and has provided interactive tools for exploring parameter choices, as well as a [video interview](https://youtu.be/n-jGPICZMR0?si=NpfyTRB88-sUxtlh) for deeper engagement. Technical discussions have focused on several operational and documentation issues. In particular, the absence of a signature mode tailored for accounting practices was noted, suggesting a gap in transaction handling features that could impact security and protocol completeness. The feasibility of stateless off-chain transactions—critical for protocols like Lightning and vaults—was debated, specifically the burden of large data requirements per signature (up to 5777 bytes), which could inflate operational costs, particularly when multiple entities must replicate unsigned states. Alternative schemes such as Falcon were identified for potential compactness, but these might expose nodes to new denial-of-service risks. Documentation usability also came under scrutiny, particularly the lack of a table of contents, which could hinder navigation and comprehension, emphasizing the ongoing need for thorough, accessible technical writing. The SHRINCS BIP is structured to define only the cryptographic scheme, following the precedent set by BIP340, without addressing deployment logistics or cost implications. For full integration into Bitcoin, an additional BIP will be required to specify consensus mechanisms and account for computational and storage costs. Comparative analysis reveals that SHRINCS signatures are substantially larger than traditional Schnorr signatures, increasing typical transaction weights by nearly fifteenfold. While this suggests higher fees, actual cost increases depend on broader market dynamics and protocol adjustments, such as block size and witness discounts. Adoption of SHRINCS could therefore reshape fee markets and network throughput, with specific impacts contingent on whether stateful or stateless signing modes are used or if alternative post-quantum algorithms are adopted. Process updates from the Bitcoin development community indicate readiness for further progress, with suggestions to use either MediaWiki or Markdown for BIP submissions and acknowledgement of GitHub’s navigational aids to improve document accessibility. There is an ongoing effort to keep documentation in standard markdown rather than GitHub-flavored markdown, ensuring coherence across platforms and future-proofing content against migration issues. The decreasing overhead associated with converting or maintaining markdown documents supports this approach, fostering consistency in the evolving Bitcoin protocol documentation landscape. Feedback collection remains integral to SHRINCS’ refinement, with the decision to delay the pull request into the BIPs repository to allow more time for community review. Notable external feedback is being tracked and considered, as seen in [Issue 21](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/issues/21) and further discussions at [x.com/P3b7_](https://x.com/P3b7_/status/2100243609861693898) and [x.com/projecteleven](https://x.com/projecteleven/status/2093450676529774992). This collaborative process aims to ensure that all relevant critiques and suggestions are incorporated before finalization. A comprehensive security analysis of SHRINCS has been published, accessible at the [Security Analysis repository](https://github.com/SHRINCS/Security-Analysis). The main paper details the full specification and EU-CMA security proof, reducing the security guarantees of SHRINCS to its underlying primitives and evaluating bounds for both classical and quantum adversaries.
